label: Amount Input
title: Amount Input
summary: Make monetary entry primary while keeping optional detail close.

anatomy.title: Amount first, note second
anatomy.description: AmountInput composes MoneyValue with NoteInput. The component passes its context to both children so their tokens resolve together.
blocks: The currency symbol gives the amount a clear unit.
MoneyValue is the primary editable value and owns its view/edit behavior.
NoteInput is optional supporting detail that becomes useful when focused or filled.

anatomy.note: The currency symbol gives the amount a clear unit.
MoneyValue is the primary editable value and owns its view/edit behavior.
NoteInput is optional supporting detail that becomes useful when focused or filled.

configuration.title: Use the default children or supply focused slots
configuration.description: The component exposes two slots and an owning context. Choose the currency and child values through MoneyValue and NoteInput.
blocks: Omitted slots fall back to MoneyValue and NoteInput children.
Adapt the detail to the task
Supply children when the entry needs another currency or note wording.

states.title: Let each child own its interaction state
states.description: MoneyValue supplies view and edit behavior through its props. NoteInput responds to focus and controlled text; its internal state is runtime-driven.
blocks: Use the quiet view when the amount is not being edited.
Tap the amount to enter the inline edit behavior.
A short controlled note stays supporting detail.

sizing.title: Respect natural content size
sizing.description: AmountInput uses the children’s natural size. Currency, amount length, note text, and the owning context affect the rendered width; avoid forcing an unbroken value into a narrow host.
blocks: Give the amount and note enough room to stay legible.
Short content keeps the natural Hug-sized children readable.

content.title: Make the unit and note easy to understand
content.description: Currency belongs with the amount. Notes add supporting detail and should remain short enough to scan beside the primary value.
blocks: Keep the symbol or code visible so the amount does not depend on surrounding copy.
Use a short phrase that explains the reason or destination.
Show the amount precision the decision needs, without an unbroken string that cannot fit.

inContext.title: Support a transfer review
inContext.description: Place the amount entry in a Card or review composition so the person knows what they are completing.
blocks: A Card gives the entry a task context while AmountInput keeps amount primary.
specimen: Enter the amount and an optional note before sending.

doDont.title: Keep amount primary and detail supporting
doDont.description: The visual pairs use child choices and show the visible consequence of each content choice.
blocks: The amount reads as a monetary value immediately.
Without a currency, the number needs surrounding copy to become meaningful.
A concise reason remains secondary to the amount.
Write a note that takes over
An oversized note competes with the primary amount and makes the natural width harder to manage.
The displayed precision fits the entry’s purpose.
An unbroken string clips inside a narrow teaching frame; widen the host or choose a meaningful precision.

sources.title: Grounded in the public amount-entry contract
sources.description: This guide uses the published AmountInput API, the inspected Figma master, and the canonical Storybook fixtures.
blocks: Examples use public AmountInput, MoneyValue, and NoteInput exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. The owner passes Context3=Amount Input with Color Mode=Light to reproduce the inspected Figma context. Storybook’s default fixture relies on ambient context and renders smaller typography than the Figma parent; the guide labels the owner context choice instead of claiming those defaults are identical. The NoteInput state prop is accepted but unused by the implementation; its visible editing state is focus-driven.
